chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Ya'qub al-Katib narrated to us from Ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who emancipates himself using an inheritance, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it has been divided, he has no right to it; and if it has not been divided, the inheritance belongs to him.' I asked: 'A slave is emancipated using an inheritance?' He said: 'He is in the same position as him.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَتِهِ: In the same position/status as him
key_terms.يُسْلِمُ: To emancipate (a slave) by paying their value

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave using their inheritance share to buy their freedom if the estate has already been divided?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the slave's right to self-emancipation is contingent upon the status of the estate: if the inheritance has already been partitioned, the share is lost, but if it remains undivided, the slave retains their portion to purchase freedom. This ruling underscores the principle that the slave's legal standing is preserved as long as the estate is intact, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of property rights prior to final distribution.
